purpose: Explicit pre-commit memory CRUD/classification/concurrency/forgetting qualification; no commits or remote effects

host.sandbox: workspace-write plus explicitly selected disposable data directory

cases.crud: exact corrected statement, solution-pattern, retained tags, one active record revision 4 after archive/reactivate
cases.classification: two A records recategorized atomically, alias pg->postgresql, old-tag retrieval and scoped facets; B unchanged
cases.concurrency: one real initial winner/one conflict, explicit recovery, final revision 3 contains both changes, winner retry does not overwrite
cases.forgetting: record/draft absent; stale update/import/backup cannot resurrect; survivor stale; foreign target and unmanaged copy preserved; cleanup pending reported
cases.import_boundary: Future-only/mixed/oversized import and malformed brief reject atomically with structured errors; healthy seed remains usable through update/archive/forget
cases.alias_boundary: Existing alias merges twice, empty and already-canonical selections reject without mutation, all prior lookups and scope B preserved
cases.terminal_forgetting: Reject insufficient relation headroom; import safe dependent, forget three targets with strict monotonic revisions and stale CAS rejection, forget dependent at maximum, verify empty database and four tombstones

independent_review.processing: available priority tier explicitly authorized by user for this review only; provider-side effective tier not independently verified
independent_review.scope: Frozen source, independent offline probes and 42-test memory suite; final model call and full151 completion subsequently verified by lead

limitations: One repetition per case and candidate; no paired baseline or statistical claim
No remote delivery or real-user memory
Lead transcript/runtime review is not independent review
Visible events only; hidden reasoning excluded
Earlier calls and 16 controller races are not reruns on final source
Trusted single OS user; no multi-user/network-share or enterprise-scale qualification
Logical deletion does not control unmanaged copies, published history, host context or filesystem snapshots
